Presentation · Grammar

Plans, but not promises

One stable form for future possibilities.

7 min
03

Your task

Study the pattern and examples.

Then correct the two crossed-out mistakes aloud and explain each correction.

The form never changes.

subject + may / might + base verb

I may visit my family.   She might go cycling.
We might not stay at home.

won’t0%
mightpossible
maypossible
willcertain
01
No “to”
I might to go go out.
02
No -s
She may visits visit us.
03
Negative
may not / might not + base verb
04
Meaning
Both express possibility. Might can sound less certain.
Concept check
Is the plan certain? No. Does the verb change after may? No. Can we say might to go? No.

Practice · Accuracy

The polished sentence

Focus on form and degree of certainty.

8 min
05

Your task

Choose one option in every sentence.

Complete all eight items, then press “Check answers” to see your score.

1. I’m not sure. I ___ at home tonight.

2. Ella may ___ her family on Sunday.

3. The weather looks bad, so we ___ cycling.

4. I haven’t decided. I ___ do yoga later.

5. She ___ at home, but she isn’t certain.

6. Which plan is certain?

7. We ___ our friends if they are free.

8. It is possible that he won’t go out.

Word bank

Your sentence

Track 6.10 · Pronunciation

Hear the rhythm

The modal is light and unstressed. The activity phrase carries the meaning. Listen, then repeat each full idea without breaking the phrase.

Listen for the structure

may / might + base verb
I may VISIT my FAMILY.
I might GO OUT in the EVENING.

Production · Personal planning

Your flexible weekend

Create a realistic plan that can change.

12 min
07

Your task

Write and present a flexible weekend plan.

Use four weekend phrases and at least three examples of may or might.

Your situation

You have a free weekend, but the weather may change.
MorningWhat might you do?
AfternoonWhat may change?
EveningWhat might you avoid?

Speak for 60–90 seconds. Use four weekend phrases and three examples of may/might.

Teacher note
Do not interrupt the first attempt. Note one excellent collocation and one form to repair. Then change the scenario and ask the student to adapt two plans immediately.
